The post that reached the most people wasn't the post people talked about.

I ranked four weeks of LinkedIn analytics and last month's Shashi.co traffic the same way, by reach and by reaction. The winners didn't match.

It was the same pattern on both places.

 A post on exposure management for CISOs reached 24,394 impressions and 78 engagements.

A post about being named a Distinguished Analyst for 2027 pulled 1,191 engagements on 6,211 impressions. 

A quarter the reach, fifteen times the interaction.

Impressions follow the topic:

- Identity infrastructure and AI security
- Agentic AI in enterprise work management
- Cloudflare's FedRAMP authorization
- Nokia's fixed wireless access sale

7502026947024191488.author: Preetham Gowda
7502026947024191488.text:
Taalas is etching models into silicon and Etched is hardwiring Transformers. We are in real-time witnessing the collapse of long-standing abstraction layers. Efficiency is eating flexibility.

The same collapse is overdue in org design. Microservice-aligned teams can turn into human equivalent of the memory wall in large organizations. When one feature spans multiple services, delivery velocity slowly dies under endless alignment time. We must collapse these team abstractions into vertically integrated, virtual teams hardwired directly to customer outcomes. In a world where code generation is fast and inexpensive, operational excellence builds the ultimate moat. So we must execute this shift
